title: Current Issues
description:
The cards rendered into the #issues section (Explore More -> Current Issues). Nine at the time of the audit. Text fields accept a safe HTML subset (, , ,
) and {{fact:}} tokens; anything else is escaped and unknown tags fail the build.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema file, so editors validate on save.

section_intro.description: Lead paragraph above the grid. Should carry a {{fact:issues-last-updated}} token rather than a literal month -- the audit found this saying 'September 2026' while the footer said 'June 2026'.

issues.description: DISPLAY ORDER IS ARRAY ORDER. There is deliberately no 'order' field: a second source of ordering is a second thing to keep in sync.

rag_only_issues.description: Canonical matched_issue values that have no issue card on the page but are still tagged on stored articles, so they must survive into KNOWN_ISSUES. 'debt' and 'rising taxes' split one card two ways; 'stormwater' and 'Siwanoy expansion' have no card at all.

rag_order.description: Emission order for the generated KNOWN_ISSUES map. This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: matchIssue scores by the LONGEST matching keyword and breaks ties by iteration order, and many keywords across different issues are the same length ('colonial' and 'flooding' are both 8). Reordering can therefore change which issue a question routes to. Pinned to the order the map was written in by hand so the switch to generation changed no routing. The build fails if this list does not exactly cover the generated keys.

id.description: Stable kebab-case slug. Becomes the card's DOM id and anchor target, and is the key the RAG pipeline tags Examiner articles against. Never renumber or reword -- inbound links and article tags break.

title.description: Card headline (h3). Plain text, no markup.

status.description: Drives the coloured dot: renders as CSS class .dot-<value>. Only these three exist in the stylesheet. Adding a fourth (e.g. 'urgent') requires adding matching CSS first, or the dot renders unstyled.

status_label.description: The sentence beside the dot, e.g. 'Active -- board weighing appointment vs. referendum; October meeting scheduled'. Free text: it is a status summary, not a repeat of the enum.

tag.description: The words printed on the chip: 'Budget / Taxes', 'Personnel', 'Elections'. Deliberately NOT the same as tag_style -- the audit found tag-budget carrying three different labels and tag-energy carrying two.

tag_style.description: Chip colour only: renders as CSS class .tag-<value>. Many labels share one style; that is intended. Must match an existing .tag-<value> rule.

description.description: Card body copy. Safe HTML subset plus {{fact:<id>}} tokens -- write {{fact:village-budget-fy2627}}, never a literal dollar figure.

governing_body.description: Foreign keys to bodies.json ids. An ARRAY because issues span bodies: the EMS station is Town + Village, the Con Ed rate case is Village + County. Build fails on an id with no matching body.

last_updated.description: When a human last reviewed this card against its source (YYYY-MM-DD). Surfaced by the build as a staleness warning.

keywords.description: Retrieval hints for the Ask Pelham RAG step -- names, places and phrases a resident might type that do not appear verbatim in the title. Not rendered.

prompt_caution.description: A jurisdiction or attribution warning emitted whenever the generated prompt discusses this issue, e.g. 'This is a PELHAM MANOR matter -- NOT the Village of Pelham and NOT the Town of Pelham.' Pelham's layered government makes misattribution the most likely factual error the assistant can make, and tests/ai.spec.js already asserts the Amtrak/Forest Road case specifically. Attached to the issue rather than the prompt template so it is retired together with the issue.

show_on_home.description: False hides the card from the grid while keeping it in the file (resolved issues worth retaining for the AI and for history). Hidden issues still feed the system prompt.

rag_issue.description: The CANONICAL issue name as stored in the Supabase articles.matched_issue column, e.g. 'Picture House'. This is not a label and must not be tidied: check_examiner.py in the companion repo writes these exact strings, so renaming one silently stops matching every article already stored under the old spelling. Null when no article has ever been tagged with this issue — inventing a key would only produce a filter that matches nothing.

rag_keywords.description: Lowercase keywords that route a reader's question to this issue, emitted into KNOWN_ISSUES. Deliberately separate from `keywords`: that field is editorial description, while these are tuned against the longest-match-wins algorithm in matchIssue, so generic words are excluded on purpose — 'redevelopment' here would pull EMS-station questions onto the Picture House.

link_to.description: Where the homepage preview's 'Read more' sends the reader. Some issues are better served by a topic page than by their own card — a tax or budget issue lands on /taxes, an election issue on /elections. Null routes to the issue's anchor on /issues, which is the right default for anything without a natural home.

sources.description: Where the card comes from, oldest first, rendered as one link per entry. An array rather than a single source_url because the editorial rule is that where possible the two most recent sources are cited -- on a contested topic, citing only one side of an exchange misrepresents it. A single-source issue is a one-element array.

url.description: Article, document or recording. May be a site-relative path for an internal destination. Never a site front page -- the build rejects those.

label.description: Link text. Names the outlet and the date so two sources on one card are distinguishable at a glance.

date.description: Publication date, ISO. Null where the source carries none.
